# Callouts and code blocks {short-title="Callouts and code"}

Callouts allow important information to be highlighted. Code blocks allow code to be
displayed or executed. This chapter presents both with examples drawn from a doctoral
context.

## The five callout types {#sec-callouts}

Quarto defines five callout types, each with a precise semantic:

````markdown
::: {.callout-specification}
## Title (optional) of the callout
Content of the callout, with `specification` taking one of the values
`note`, `tip`, `warning`, `important`, or `caution`, each associated with
a colour code and an icon in the callout header.
:::
````

### `callout-note` — neutral information

````markdown
::: {.callout-note}
## Jury composition

A Cnam thesis jury comprises at minimum a chair, two reviewers
(with {{< acrs hdr >}}) and one or two examiners. The defence lasts approximately
45 minutes of presentation, followed by questions from the jury.
:::
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

::: {.callout-note}
## Jury composition

A Cnam thesis jury comprises at minimum a chair, two reviewers
(with {{< acrs hdr >}}) and one or two examiners. The defence lasts approximately
45 minutes of presentation, followed by questions from the jury.
:::
:::

### `callout-tip` — actionable advice

````markdown
::: {.callout-tip}
## Start writing early

Start writing your thesis from the second year of doctoral study. Late writing is
the primary cause of exceeding the contractual thesis duration. Even imperfect drafts
are better than empty sections.
:::
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

::: {.callout-tip}
## Start writing early

Start writing your thesis from the second year of doctoral study. Late writing is
the primary cause of exceeding the contractual thesis duration. Even imperfect drafts
are better than empty sections.
:::
:::

### `callout-warning` — pitfall to avoid

````markdown
::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not rename chapters without updating the profile

If you rename a `.qmd` file, update the `chapters:` list in
`_quarto-en.yml` (or `_quarto-fr.yml`). Quarto does not automatically detect
missing files and will fail silently.
:::
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not rename chapters without updating the profile

If you rename a `.qmd` file, update the `chapters:` list in
`_quarto-en.yml` (or `_quarto-fr.yml`). Quarto does not automatically detect
missing files and will fail silently.
:::
:::

### `callout-important` — non-negotiable point

````markdown
::: {.callout-important}
## PDF/A-1b mandatory for theses.fr

The {{< acrs abes >}} requires a PDF/A for archiving on theses.fr. This template
automatically generates a PDF/A-1b via `\usepackage[a-1b]{pdfx}`. Do not remove
this package from the template.
:::
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

::: {.callout-important}
## PDF/A-1b mandatory for theses.fr

The {{< acrs abes >}} requires a PDF/A for archiving on theses.fr. This template
automatically generates a PDF/A-1b via `\usepackage[a-1b]{pdfx}`. Do not remove
this package from the template.
:::
:::

### `callout-caution` — danger with consequences

````markdown
::: {.callout-caution}
## Do not use `date:` for the defence date

Quarto interprets the `date:` key as a JavaScript date and produces
"Invalid Date" for French date strings (e.g. "12 June 2026"). Use exclusively
the custom key `date-soutenance:` provided in this template.
:::
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

::: {.callout-caution}
## Do not use `date:` for the defence date

Quarto interprets the `date:` key as a JavaScript date and produces
"Invalid Date" for French date strings (e.g. "12 June 2026"). Use exclusively
the custom key `date-soutenance:` provided in this template.
:::
:::

## Callouts with title and collapsing {#sec-callouts-options}

The title is added with a `## Title` line inside the callout (as in the examples
above). To make a callout collapsed by default (click to open), use the `collapse`
attribute:

````markdown
::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Click to see the tip (collapsed by default)

This callout is collapsed when the HTML document opens. In PDF, it always appears
in full (collapsing is an HTML-only feature).
:::
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Click to see the tip (collapsed by default)

This callout is collapsed when the HTML document opens. In PDF, it always appears
in full (collapsing is an HTML-only feature).
:::
:::

## Code blocks — display only {#sec-code-display}

To display code without executing it, use either a block delimited by backticks without
a language specifier in curly braces, or a chunk with `eval: false`:

````markdown
```python
# This block is displayed but not executed
import numpy as np
x = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
print(x.mean())
```
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

```python
# This block is displayed but not executed
import numpy as np
x = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
print(x.mean())
```
:::

To display the code of an executable chunk without executing it (useful for installation
or configuration examples):

````markdown
```{{python}}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
# Installing dependencies
pip install matplotlib numpy pandas
```
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

::: {#c1284b9b .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# Installing template dependencies
# pip install matplotlib numpy pandas
```
:::


:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Most useful chunk options

| Option | Values | Effect |
|:-------|:--------|:------|
| `echo` | `true`/`false` | shows or hides the code |
| `eval` | `true`/`false` | executes or skips the code |
| `output` | `true`/`false` | shows or hides the output |
| `warning` | `true`/`false` | shows or hides warnings |
| `fig-cap` | text | caption for the produced figure |
| `label` | `fig-...` or `tbl-...` | identifier for cross-reference |

: Frequently used Quarto chunk options. {#tbl-chunk-options}
:::

## Code blocks — with Python execution {#sec-code-exec}

In this document, all executable code examples — including the matplotlib figures of
@sec-fig-python — use `#| echo: true` to display both the source code and the result.
In a finalised thesis, code is generally hidden by switching to `#| echo: false`: only
the figure or table appears, without the code that produced it.

::: {.callout-note}
## Languages natively supported by Quarto

Quarto supports three scientific computing languages **without additional configuration**:
**Python**, **R**, and **Julia**. The chunk option syntax
(`#| echo:`, `#| fig-cap:`, etc.) and the cross-reference mechanism (`#| label:`)
are identical for all three languages. This document illustrates Python only.

Official documentation:

- Python: <https://quarto.org/docs/computations/python.html>
- R: <https://quarto.org/docs/computations/r.html>
- Julia: <https://quarto.org/docs/computations/julia.html>
:::

A Python chunk with `eval: true` (the default) executes the code and displays the
output. Here is an example with `pandas`:

````markdown
```{{python}}
#| echo: true
#| label: tbl-pandas
#| tbl-cap: "Descriptive statistics of trigonometric functions."
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Markdown

x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 1000)
df = pd.DataFrame({r'$\sin(x)$':           np.sin(x),
                   r'$\cos(x)$':           np.cos(x),
                   r'$\tan(x)$ (clipped)': np.clip(np.tan(x), -5, 5)})
Markdown(df.describe().round(3).to_markdown())
```
````

::: {.render-demo}
**Output:**

::: {#tbl-pandas .cell tbl-cap='Descriptive statistics of trigonometric functions.' execution_count=2}

::: {.callout-note}
## `freeze: auto` in `_quarto.yml`

With `execute: freeze: auto`, Quarto stores cell results in `_freeze/` and only
recomputes them if the chunk code has changed. This considerably speeds up successive
renders for theses with many computations.
:::

::: {.callout-caution}
## Remember to version the `_freeze/` folder

If you version your thesis on GitHub and want reviewers to be able to compile without
Python installed, commit the `_freeze/` folder. The cached results are stored there
and will be used instead of re-executing the code.
:::
